Hi Priya / Alex —

Quick note ahead of your April renewal (term ends 2026-04-30). Based on our usage patterns and your expansion ask during last week’s call, we put together a recommended amendment that adds dedicated GPU pools in EU and APAC, plus updated throughput guarantees and a failover plan. High level proposal: 

- EU dedicated pool: 8x A100 (80GB) reserved GPUs — configured as two sub-pools for London and Frankfurt, active-active routing for low latency.
- APAC dedicated pool: 4x A100 (80GB) reserved GPUs — primary in Singapore, warm-standby in Sydney for failover.
- Throughput guarantees: pooled throughput targets of 3.2k tokens/sec EU, 1.6k tokens/sec APAC (sustained) with autoscaling burst capacity for periodic spikes.
- Latency SLOs: target P95 < 120ms for 256-token generations; P99 < 250ms under steady state for EU/ APAC region-local traffic.
- Failover: automatic geo-fallback to nearest region with traffic shaping and preserved KV cache for warm replicas; cross-region cold-start window estimated 45–120s depending on model.

Attached is a draft amendment capturing the new committed capacity, pricing impact, and a migration runbook. Can you confirm: (1) the proposed GPU counts/regions meet your latency targets, (2) whether you want active-active across EU sites or single EU region, and (3) acceptable timing for a staged migration (we recommend a 4-week window with canary routing).

If it helps I can loop in Vivek for any compliance notes specific to EU data residency. Next steps: once we align, we’ll issue a redlined amendment + DocuSign.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the detailed draft. A few clarifying questions from product & procurement while we review the attachment: 

1) Latency expectations: the P95/P99 numbers look reasonable, but we need to understand worst-case tail during failover. Can you provide historical failover surface area and an estimated RTO for active-passive vs active-active?

2) Cold-starts & KV cache: our inference load is very prefix-heavy for certain workflows; preserving KV cache is critical. How will you manage cache warming across regions without incurring large egress or prolonged stalls?

3) Pricing impact: rough delta to committed monthly spend for the proposed counts, plus what the per-token/embedding price will be for traffic routed cross-region during failover. Procurement copied for visibility.

4) Security/compliance: we will require a note in the amendment about EU data residency and where logs/metrics are stored. We’ll likely request Vivek or your security contact to provide a short attestation for the amendment.

Can Neha or Dylan drop a short technical runbook section that has expected RTO/P95/P99 during failover scenarios? That will speed our internal sign-off.

Subject: Re: Renewal: proposed multi-region Dedicated expansion (EU + APAC) – technical clarifications

Hi Priya — quick technical note to answer the runbook ask. Below are realistic operational expectations based on the models/workloads we ran in your staging cluster: 

Summary (technical):
- Cache & warm-up: we use prefix-aware KV caching. For workloads where 70–80% of requests share prefixes, a warm replica can deliver ~90% of steady-state latency within 30–90s of traffic routing. Full KV warm (all prefixes) can take longer (~10–30 min) dependent on corpus size.
- Cold-start (no warm replicas): first inference wave may experience elevated P95 (up to 600–900ms) for 1024-token generations, then stabilize.
- Active-active EU split: recommended for <100ms median for EU users. Active-active reduces failover RTO to ~5–15s for routing changes, assuming balanced traffic and shared healthchecks.
- Active-passive EU (single active region): quicker initial deploy but RTO for full capacity may be 45–120s as GPUs and KV caches warm.
- Throughput numbers (observed): each A100 80GB in our config sustains ~400–500 tokens/sec for encoder-only & smaller gen models; for large causal models with KV overhead expect ~250–350 tokens/sec per GPU. We modeled 8x A100 EU -> pooled steady throughput ~= 2,400–3,000 tokens/sec.
- Latency SLOs (realistic targets): P95 < 120ms (256 tokens) for active-active; P99 can spike to 220–300ms under heavy load or during autoscale events.
- Cross-region egress: we advise limiting cross-region failover to short windows; egress cost and increased latency will apply.

Operational suggestions:
- Canary plan: 3-week rollout: week 1 (internal canary 5% traffic), week 2 (10–25% for EU region load tests), week 3 (full cutover).
- Pre-warm script: Redwood will run controlled pre-warm traffic for top 200 prompt templates prior to final cutover to reduce KV cold penalty.
- Monitoring: we’ll add per-route p95/p99 dashboards and automatic rollback on latency regressions.

I’ll attach a short CSV with the canonical throughput measurements and a snippet of the runbook to the amendment. Happy to review with your infra team live if helpful.

—Neha

Commercial outline:
- Term: 12 months (2026-05-01 to 2027-04-30) with annual true-up.
- Committed GPUs: EU 8x A100 (reserved), APAC 4x A100 (reserved).
- Monthly committed spend delta: $96,000/month (this includes reserved GPU base + baseline throughput licensing). Exact line items in attached amendment.
- Discount: 18% off list for a full-commit 12-month term.
- Migration credit: one-time $25,000 credit applied to first invoice to offset migration costs if amendment signed by 2026-03-31.
- Pricing during failover: cross-region requests billed at the same per-token rate up to 10% of monthly traffic; above that we will apply a 25% premium to cover egress/replication costs.

Next steps: I’ll push a redline of the PDF with the commercial table. If procurement can sign off on the timeline (we need LOI or signature by 2026-03-31 to lock the migration credit), we’ll route the DocuSign today. Link will be sent once Marissa confirms final counts and Vivek signs the compliance note.

Thanks — Rishi
